### 2026-10-11 – I searched for the issue and found the solution .

**1h**

I searched for the issue and found the solution .

The problem was this -

![arduino error](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/gSMICPeKfFIX4r61sX8jLHHguUkM0Btr/67f579599aaf62f4c1ba3ece02ce1c6f750efb1d5ee22fe2550c2eed466325b9.png)

Here is what I found and did -
 1. Cleared the corrupted files
  2. Downloaded and unpacked ESP32 Core v2.0.17
  3. Extracted all compilers and utility binaries:
      • riscv32-esp-elf-gcc (the native compiler for the ESP32-C3)
      • xtensa-esp32-elf-gcc
      • esptool_py (v4.5.1)
      • mkspiffs & mklittlefs
  4. Placed the core files directly into 2.0.17.
  5. Appended boardsmanager.additional.urls=https://espressif.github.io/arduino-esp32/package_esp32_index.json into preferences.txt:72 so Arduino IDE retains the link permanently.
  Because this was written directly into the container directory that Arduino IDE reads, the IDE immediately
  recognizes XIAO_ESP32C3 under Tools → Board → ESP32 Arduino.
Here us the proof -

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/gSMICPeKfFIX4r61sX8jLHHguUkM0Btr/dc02565d3c113f510f82fd2093127560dac0864d110d0c1bacfa08fbaaf7bb89.png)

### 2026-10-11 – I finished writing the full code for Starbie.ino .

**2.33h**

I finished writing the full code for Starbie.ino .
Here is what i added and the highlights :

  I used millis() instead of delay() to prevent freezing of the microcontroller as it halts the process for a moment. Instead I used millis() to check elapsed time and let the loop refersh the display after intervals while reading sensors in the background.

Switches can sometime cause mutiple click due to bouncing to avoid this , i defined a function wasPressed() with 30 sec pause after every detection of pressing of the button avoiding accidental clicks.

 In setup() , i  kept Wire.begin(I2C_SDA_PIN,  I2C_SCL_PIN)  on GPIO 6 and GPIO 7  .
This lets the SSD1306 OLED DISPLAY listen at address 0x3C, while the MPU 6050 listens to 0x68 whille sharing the same two copper wire on the PCB.

  I added logic to detect the tilt of Starbie precisely, accordingly choose mode - NAP,PLAY,FEED and used 3d pythagorean theorem to get the total 3d force vector giving the exact amount of shake . I added a deadzone to avoid accidental canging of state. I also took in account gravitational accleration .

 I used the ESP32's built-in non volatile memory (Preferences,h) in savePet() and loadPet(). This enables Starbie to restore its stats in flash  even when it is unplugged.

  I set up the logic for switch 2 for showing live dashboard whenever pressed to show the progress bars for JOY,ENERGY,FULLNESS along with live temperature , humidity obtained  from DH11 sensor .
